query: Why are Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs) not eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme?
reference_answer: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is only for Singaporean lower-wage workers.If you require financial assistance, please contact theComCarehotline at 1800-222-0000, or emailAsk_SSO@msf.gov.sg.
context:
[Document 1]
All types of properties e.g. Housing & Development Board flat, private property and non-residential property, are taken into account in determining the eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.

[Document 2]
The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is only for Singaporean lower-wage workers.If you require financial assistance, please contact theComCarehotline at 1800-222-0000, or emailAsk_SSO@msf.gov.sg.

[Document 3]
Basic salary, overtime pay, and bonuses are part of a worker’s total income that will help support the worker and his or her family. Given that the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is intended to supplement the income of lower-wage workers, it is most useful to assess the total income in determining one’s eligibility for WIS.

[Document 4]
Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) is based on your net trade income earned in the work year and does not include previous year's losses.

[Document 5]
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, regardless of household income and Annual Value of their residences, are automatically eligible.
answer: Singapore Permanent Residents (PRs) are not eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme because the scheme is specifically designed for Singaporean lower-wage workers, and PRs are not considered Singapore citizens [Document 5]. Additionally, the WIS considers total income, which excludes PRs' income since they are not Singapore citizens [Document 4].
